function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**Reykjavík – Iceland’s Ice‑Hockey Hub** | Why Reykjavík is the top choice | Details | |---------------------------------|---------| | **Home of the National Team** | The Icelandic national team (the “Icelandic Penguins”) trains and plays its home games in Reykjavík. The city hosts the national championships and international fixtures. | | **Facilities** | • **Laugardalsvöllur (Laugardalur Ice Hall)** – The largest indoor rink in Iceland, used for league games, training camps, and public skating.
• **Hraunsholtsskóli Ice Rink** – A modern arena that hosts youth and adult leagues. | | **Local Teams** | • **Íþróttafélagið Fram** – One of Iceland’s oldest clubs, with a strong hockey program.
• **KR (Knattspyrnufélag Reykjavíkur)** – Offers competitive teams across age groups. | | **Events & Tournaments** | • **Icelandic Hockey League (Úrvalsdeild)** – The premier domestic competition, with playoffs and finals held in Reykjavík.
• **International Youth Tournaments** – Reykjavík often hosts Nordic youth championships and friendly matches. | | **Accessibility** | • **Capital City** – Easy to reach via Keflavík International Airport.
• **Public Transport** – Buses and taxis connect the city’s rinks and hotels. | | **Cultural Experience** | Combine hockey with Reykjavík’s vibrant nightlife, museums, and the famous geothermal Blue Lagoon nearby. | ### Quick Tips for Visiting 1. **Book a Game** – Check the Úrvalsdeild schedule; catching a local match is a great way to see Icelandic hockey culture. 2. **Ice Skating Lessons** – Many rinks offer beginner lessons; a quick session can be a fun way to warm up before the game. 3. **Stay Near the Rink** – Hotels like the **Hotel Borg** or **Radisson Blu** are within walking distance of Laugardalsvöllur. 4. **Explore the City** – After the game, stroll through Laugardalur Park, visit the National Museum, or enjoy a hot chocolate at a local café. --- **Bottom line:** Reykjavík is the heart of Icelandic ice hockey, offering the best combination of facilities, teams, events, and accessibility. If you’re looking to immerse yourself in Iceland’s hockey scene, Reykjavík is the city to choose.
